record.field: Runs a time-based automation right now, exactly as its schedule would: spawns an duplicate of the agent that executes the actions instructions in a headless run, and shows the result of it in the chat. Use it when the user asks to run, test or try an automation now, instead of ever executing the automation's steps yourself in the conversation. Only time-based automations (scheduled actions and time rules) can run on demand; an event-based rule is tested by creating or updating a record that matches its trigger. After creating a time-based automation, offer the user to run it once by CALLING this tool right away: its confirmation card ("Run" / "Not now") is the offer. Never ask "should I run it?" in your message text instead, that leaves the user without the Run button.
AI Tool: Create or Update Automation
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_create_update_automation(ai, automation_id, name, description, active, trigger, ai_action_prompt, explanation)

Create and update persistent automations for actions you should perform later, repeatedly or in response to record event. Use this tool when the user asks you to perform an action or send a reminder at a future time, on a recurring schedule, or when records are created, changed, deleted, messaged, or meet specified conditions. When creating a new automation, `name`, `description`, `trigger`, `ai_action_prompt` and `explanation` are required. When editing an existing automation, `automation_id` and `explanation` are required. For the other parameters, only provide the ones that need to be updated. ## Trigger type Prefer the time-based triggers (`on_time_created`, `on_time_updated`, `on_time`) over the synchronous ones (`on_create`, `on_create_or_write`): they run shortly after the event instead of during the user's save. "When a ticket is created, …" is `on_time_created` with a 1 minute delay; "whenever a lead is updated, …" is `on_time_updated`. Use `on_create` / `on_create_or_write` only when the user explicitly asks for an immediate, synchronous action, or for a transition on specific fields that needs `filter_pre_domain`. ## Trigger examples - Tag every new ticket (preferred creation trigger): `{"trigger": {"type": "on_time_created", "target_model": "helpdesk.ticket", "date_offset_or_interval": {"amount": 1, "unit": "minutes"}}}` - Trigger when the tag "Bug" is added on my tasks (a field transition, hence `on_create_or_write`): `{"trigger": {"type": "on_create_or_write", "observed_fields": ["tag_ids"], "filter_pre_domain": "[('tag_ids', 'not in', ['Bug'])]", "filter_domain": "[('tag_ids', 'in', ['Bug']), ('user_id', '=', 3)]"}}` (if the ID of the user is 3). - Trigger the day before the expected closing date: `{"trigger": {"type": "on_time", "observed_fields": "date_deadline", "date_offset_or_interval": {"direction": "before", "amount": 1, "unit": "day"}}}` - Trigger on creation if the record is unassigned: `{"trigger": {"type": "on_time_created", "filter_domain": "[('user_id', '=', False)]", "date_offset_or_interval": {"amount": 5, "unit": "minutes"}}}` - Trigger on each Monday: `{"trigger": {"type": "on_schedule", "date_offset_or_interval": {"amount": 7, "unit": "day", "next_trigger_date": "2026-08-24 09:00:00"}}}` (if next Monday is 2026-08-24)
